extraction.name: MINT-1T: Scaling Open-Source Multimodal Data by 10x: A Multimodal Dataset with One Trillion Tokens
extraction.description: MINT-1T, the most extensive and diverse open-source Multimodal INTerleaved dataset to date. MINT-1T comprises of one trillion text tokens and 3.4 billion images, a 10x scale-up from existing open-source datasets. Additionally, we include previously untapped sources such as PDFs and ArXiv papers.
extraction.creator: Anas Awadalla, Le Xue, Oscar Lo, Manli Shu, Hannah Lee, Etash Guha, Matt Jordan, Sheng Shen, Mohamed Awadalla, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Ran Xu, Yejin Choi, Ludwig Schmidt
extraction.publisher: University of Washington, Salesforce Research, Stanford University, University of Texas at Austin, University of Califomia, Berkeley
extraction.citeAs: Anas Awadalla et al. MINT-1T: Scaling Open-Source Multimodal Data by 10x: A Multimodal Dataset with One Trillion Tokens. arXiv:2406.11271v5 [cs.CV], 31 Oct 2024.
extraction.isLiveDataset: Yes the dataset will be updated by the authors of this work. We will communicate updates through the README in the Huggingface interface.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MINT-1T curates a large-scale open-source dataset that taps into more diverse sources of interleaved documents such as PDFs and ArXiv papers. This section outlines our methods for sourcing multimodal documents, filtering low-quality documents, deduplicating data, and removing not safe for work and undesirable content.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: We noticed two limitations with using the PyMuPDF package for parsing PDFs: 1) we sometimes are unable to detect images 2) as PDFs have arbitrary layouts, in some cases we extract an incorrect reading order (see Figure 10). This compromise between speed and accuracy is a noted limitation, and future work should focus on developing fast, robust methods for determining the reading order across diverse document layouts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: MINT-1T’s HTML documents are filtered from CommonCrawl WARC dumps from 2017 to 2024. MINT-1T PDF documents are filtered from CommonCrawl WAT dumps from 2023 to 2024. MINT-1T ArXiv documents is a subset of all ArXiv documents.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The data was collected from January 2024 to June 2024. We include web data from 2013 to 2024.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: To mitigate the risk of personal data leakage, we anonymize email addresses and IP addresses in our text data. Following FineWeb, we replace emails with templates such as "email@example.com" and IPs with randomly generated non-functional IPs.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: To remove duplicated content, we perform paragraph and document text deduplication within each CommonCrawl snapshot and image deduplication to remove repetitive, uninformative images such as icons and logos. All deduplication steps are done separately for each data source.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was preprocessed to remove low quality text, duplicate documents/text portions, and remove not safe for work and low quality images. This included: parsing HTML DOM trees, extracting PDF links and reading PDFs using PyMuPDF2, building ArXiv documents from LaTeX source code using TexSoup3, eliminating non-English documents using Fasttext's language identification model (with a confidence threshold of 0.65), removing documents with URLs containing NSFW substrings, applying text filtering methods from RefinedWeb (removing excessive duplicate n-grams or low quality text), downloading and filtering images (removing non-retrievable links, images smaller than 150 pixels or larger than 20,000 pixels, and images with aspect ratios greater than two for HTML or three for PDFs), applying an NSFW image detector to discard documents with NSFW images, and performing paragraph/document/image deduplication using a Bloom Filter and SHA256 hashes.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: NSFW image detector (https://github.com/GantMan/nsfw_model), Fasttext (https://fasttext.cc/), PyMuPDF (https://github.com/pymupdf/PyMuPDF), TexSoup (https://github.com/alvinwan/TexSoup), Bloom Filter (https://github.com/allenai/bff), HTML parsing (https://github.com/huggingface/OBELICS), Text quality filters (https://github.com/huggingface/datatrove)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: This work’s authors will actively respond to issues in MINT-1T and maintain the dataset. The owners can be contacted through email or the Issues tab in the Huggingface interface. The erratum will be present on the README of the Huggingface dataset page. The dataset will be updated by the authors of this work, and updates will be communicated through the README in the Huggingface interface. Older versions of the dataset can be found using the Git history of the dataset repository, and issues with previous versions will be communicated in the erratum. Contributions to the dataset will be accepted through the Pull Request mechanism of the Huggingface interface. A Google form will be provided for opting data out of MINT-1T.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Yes, if it is present on the public web then it is possible to find images of individuals as well as text about specific individuals. We masked personally identifiable information such as emails and IP addresses to remove personal data from MINT-1T. Yes, if it is present on the public web then it is possible such data is found in MINT-1T.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: An important consideration when releasing large datasets is to avoid exposing harmful content from the web. We were careful about filtering out personally identifiable information and not safe for work content from MINT-1T. However, future work should explore more ways to improve the safety of multimodal internet data. We follow previous works in not using text quality classifier models as they have been shown to favor text from certain demographics. While we take steps to reduce biases and risks in our dataset, we encourage dataset consumers to further filter the data based on their use case.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: We follow previous works in not using text quality classifier models as they have been shown to favor text from certain demographics.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: An important consideration when releasing large datasets is to avoid exposing harmful content from the web. Future work should explore more ways to improve the safety of multimodal internet data. Subsequent work should train models on larger subsets of MINT-1T, build filtering methods to improve data quality, and curate multimodal sequences from other sources. MINT-1T is not self-contained and relies on downloading external image URLs to collect the full dataset. There are no guarantees these URLs will remain available over time as link rot is a common problem for large scale image datasets. Moreover, as this dataset is over 300TB large, it is infeasible for us to host the full datasets (with images included). We noticed two limitations with using the PyMuPDF package for parsing PDFs: 1) we sometimes are unable to detect images 2) as PDFs have arbitrary layouts, in some cases we extract an incorrect reading order. This compromise between speed and accuracy is a noted limitation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: MINT-1T is built for pre-training large multimodal models that can process multiple interleaved images and text. It fills a gap in the open-source space where there is a lack of large scale multimodal interleaved pre-training datasets. The dataset has been used to train large multimodal models to validate data quality against competitors. It can also be used for other training objectives like generating interleaved images and text sequences or for building multimodal document retrieval systems. Non-recommended uses include training models that ingest or generate personally identifying information (such as images of people’s faces and other sensitive content) as well as military applications.
